He joined Google in 2004 and was named chief executive officer of Google in October 2015 and of Alphabet in December 2019, succeeding co-founder Larry Page at the parent company.

sentences.quote: As CEO he has led product and engineering across Search, Chrome, Maps, Android, Gmail, and Google Workspace, and has refocused the company's strategy on AI.
sentences.text: He has led product and engineering for Google's products and platforms, including Search, Chrome, Maps, Android, Gmail and Google Workspace, and has refocused company strategy on artificial intelligence.

Before joining Google he worked in engineering and product management at Applied Materials and in management consulting at McKinsey & Company, after studying metallurgical engineering at IIT Kharagpur, materials science at Stanford University and business at Wharton.

mgmt_bio.text: Sundar Pichai, 53, is chief executive officer of Alphabet Inc. and of its subsidiary Google, and has served as an Alphabet director since 2017 and sits on the Executive Committee. He has led product and engineering for Google's products and platforms, including Search, Chrome, Maps, Android, Gmail and Google Workspace, and has refocused company strategy on artificial intelligence.

sentences.text: In August 2026 Alphabet announced a sweeping AI leadership overhaul: Demis Hassabis ceded the Google DeepMind CEO role to become chairman of DeepMind and chief scientist of Alphabet, Jeff Dean left after 27 years, and Koray Kavukcuoglu took over many of Hassabis's responsibilities.

Sundar Pichai's senior team otherwise remains stable, with Anat Ashkenazi as CFO, Ruth Porat as President and Chief Investment Officer, Philipp Schindler as Chief Business Officer and Kent Walker as President, Global Affairs.

sentences.quote: Google now expects capex for the year of $195 billion to $205 billion, up from the $180 billion to $190 billion forecast provided last quarter.
sentences.text: On the July 2026 call Ashkenazi lifted 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195-205 billion, having said 2027 spending should rise significantly further, and flagged greater use of third-party capacity as a bridge amid supply constraints.

sentences.text: Under Sundar Pichai, Alphabet has reoriented capital toward AI, with 2026 capital expenditure guidance of $195 billion to $205 billion, raised from an earlier $180 billion to $190 billion range, funded partly by a $20.5 billion public offering, a $10 billion private placement to a Berkshire Hathaway affiliate and a $19 billion convertible preferred sale in a single week in June.

sentences.quote: In the first half of 2026, it repurchased none, even with $69.5 billion still authorized under a buyback program its board approved in April 2025.
sentences.text: No shares were repurchased in the first half of 2026, with $69.5 billion still authorized, though the board lifted the quarterly dividend 5% to $0.22 in April 2026.

On governance, founder-controlled Class B shares carry ten votes each, and the board agreed to create a Risk and Compliance Committee after antitrust-related litigation; the 2025 search remedies ruling spared Chrome and Android from divestiture.

sentences.quote: Google Cloud revenue increased 82% year over year to $24.8 billion in second-quarter 2026.
sentences.text: Google Cloud is Alphabet's fastest-growing engine: Q2 2026 revenues rose 82% to $24.8 billion on enterprise AI solutions, AI infrastructure and core GCP services, with segment operating income more than tripling to $8.8 billion and margin reaching 35.6%.

Contracted demand is visible far ahead: Alphabet reported a $519.5 billion revenue backlog at June 30, 2026, $513.9 billion of it Google Cloud, with just over half expected to convert to revenue within 24 months.
Search advertising still funds the group, growing 17% to $63.3 billion in Q2 2026, with AI experiences driving usage and queries at an all-time high.
Subscriptions add recurring revenue, as paid subscriptions reached 350 million, led by YouTube and Google One.
